name: FULL THROTTLE
summary: An 80s spy car chase in 3 levels: biker gangs, choppers, Vegas, real fireballs.
description: You are Agent Nova Kane, and this is a movie in three levels: Bayshore, a pastel 80s beach town of art-deco hotels, palms and lifeguard towers; the Volta Chemical Works, a chemical plant at night; and the Nevada desert at dusk, the open highway to Las Vegas with the city's neon lit up on the horizon. The camera rides right behind the armed KESTREL-88, a Countach-style wedge with a double V-wing, a chrome blower and quad pipes, as you race it along a wild highway that twists, climbs over humps, leans into banked walls, rolls through a corkscrew, goes round full loops and stops dead at gaps you have to fly. Syndicate bikers, rammer sports cars, gunship SUVs, armored trucks and choppers try to finish you, and civilian traffic gets in everyone's way. The choppers drop henchmen onto your car: slam their side into the wall to scrape them off, or go upside down through a loop and they fall.

The director is on the megaphone the whole way through. Level 1 is shot as sixteen scenes, from THE GETAWAY to THE FINALE, about five to seven minutes of driving. Each one opens with a clapper slate and "ACTION!", and every few seconds he reacts to what you're doing: "Take him out, now!" when you stop shooting, "Faster, give me sparks!" when the road goes quiet, "Closer! I want paint on paint!" after a near miss, "Not the civilians!" when you hit one. Wreck the star car and he yells "CUT! Again!" and you reshoot that scene from the top. You have three reels of film for retakes.

Near misses and big kills drop into slow motion. Ramp jumps, gap jumps, loops, the corkscrew, wall rides, upside-down kills, turbo rams and multi-kills score as stunts, and the director calls every loop and jump as it comes. At the wrap he rates the take: B-Movie, Action Hero, Blockbuster or Legendary Director.

Every level you finish pays skill points: more for a better rating and for no retakes. Before the next level starts you spend them in THE GARAGE on four upgrades for the KESTREL-88, five ranks each: HANDLING (quicker steering, faster drift charge), TURBO (burns slower, refills faster), ARMOR (every hit takes less) and WEAPONS (hotter guns, one more missile per rank). Buy with Enter, A or a click, refund with Backspace, X or a right-click, and start the level from the button when you're ready. Your upgrades carry on into every run.

Wrap a level and the movie plays you its highlights: the best moments of your run (big kills, choppers coming down, henchmen slammed into the wall, big air, the boss going down, twice, from two angles) cut together from bumper, tracking, crane, aerial and kill-cam angles, in slow motion on the money shots. It plays until you press its CONTINUE button (Enter, or Start on a pad), so a stray click can't skip it. Explosions are billowing fireballs of real animated fire that light up the road and everything round them. The KESTREL is put together from its parts as you drive: the wheels turn with your speed and the fronts steer, and the body rides a light suspension, bobbing over bumps, squatting, diving, leaning through corners and drifts and slamming down on landings. It also wears its damage: it dents, scrapes, smokes, sheds parts, drags its bumper in sparks and finally burns.

Keys: the left hand drives, the right hand shoots. WASD steers, hold Shift and steer to drift (kart-style, either order; let go to boost), Space is turbo; J fires the guns, K a missile, or hold the left mouse button and right-click. Steer with the arrow keys instead and Z fires, X sends a missile. P pauses, M mutes. C (on the title or pause screen) opens the controls to change any key. Gamepads work: stick steers, A or RB drifts, X fires, B is a missile, LB or RT turbo. On the title the left and right arrows pick the level. On a phone, drag on the left to drive, hold DRIFT and steer to drift, use FIRE, MSL and TURBO, tap II to pause, and tap the level bar on the title to switch levels. Level 1 is SCENE 01, THE HIGHWAY ASSASSINATION, along the Bayshore coast road. Level 2 is THE FORMULA, in the chemical plant: twisty S-bends, banked helix ramps, loops and glass pipes the road rolls all the way round inside, so you drive the walls and the ceiling, ending with THE ALCHEMIST, whose tesla tanker fights with lightning: lane arcs, lock-on strikes and shock waves, each warned on the road first. Level 3 is ALL IN, Highway 93 across the Nevada desert at sunset: long open straights and rolling dips past Joshua trees, red rock, telephone poles, a neon motel, a lonely gas stop and casino pylons, with gaps over dry washes, two loops, a canyon corkscrew and banked walls round the red rock, and Las Vegas growing ahead of you all the way. The SNAKE EYES ride out on their choppers: outlaw bikers in leather who pull up beside your doors and whirl a chain over their heads before they swing it, so get a car's width away or slam into them sideways first. The finale is THE BIG DEALER's motorcycle carrier, a two-deck rig loaded with bikers that never stops sending them: they roll off its tail ramp, then launch off its top deck and fly at you, while it brake-checks you with its tail lights flaring. Between levels you spend skill points in the GARAGE.

The title screen plays "Bit-Beast Dash" on a loop, and it fades out as the clapper comes down on a race. All three levels are scored with "Pixel Adventure", our own song, looping under the action: it drops back whenever the director calls a line or something big blows up, so you always hear the cue. M turns all sound off, music included.

The look is cel-shaded with ink outlines: the car, the Syndicate, the traffic, the hotels, palms and skyline, the plant's tanks, gas spheres, stacks, towers, pipework and vats, and the desert's choppers, the carrier, Joshua trees, rocks, buttes, poles, motel, gas stop, casino pylons and the Las Vegas skyline were modelled and rendered in Unreal Engine 5, and the road, sky, sea, chemical lake and glass pipes are painted to match. The game lights it all: sun and moon on the banked road, haze in the distance, floodlight and headlight pools at night, glowing lights, fire and lightning; since 1.4 the fireballs and flames are rendered in Unreal too, bloom and a film grade.

whatsNew: Skill points and THE GARAGE: every level you finish pays skill points, and before the next level starts you spend them on HANDLING, TURBO, ARMOR and WEAPONS (five ranks each, refundable any time), with the keyboard, the mouse or a gamepad. The highlight reel can't be skipped by accident any more: clicks and stray keys do nothing, it plays again from the top, and only its CONTINUE button (Enter, Start on a pad, or a click on it) moves on.
